title: What if you move your ball while searching?
question: If you accidentally move your ball while searching for it in the rough, what must you do according to the Rules of Golf?

choices.text: Replace it as close as possible to its original spot, with no penalty
Take a penalty stroke and play from where it stops

explanation: If you move your ball by accident while searching, you must replace it on its original spot without penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What should you do if you move your ball while looking for it?
juniorVersion.question: You are looking for your golf ball in the long grass. Oops! You accidentally move it. What should you do?

choices.text: Leave your ball where it ended up
Put your ball back where it was, with no penalty
Add a penalty and play your ball from where it stopped
Drop a different ball and keep playing

juniorVersion.explanation: If you move your ball while you are looking for it, put it back where it was. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: This is when you have to add extra shots to your score for breaking a rule.
To put your ball back to the place where it was before.
The place where your golf ball was before it moved.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Practise putting your ball back in the right place if you move it while searching, so you learn to remember the spot.
likelyMisconceptions: Some players think you must take a penalty if you move your ball, but there is no penalty if you are just looking for it.
Some might believe you can leave your ball where it rolls to, but you must put it back.
